title.narrative: Coordination of public/private partnership and promoting access to universal birth registration in Côte d’Ivoire

description.narrative: This project supported UNICEF Côte d'Ivoire and national partners to strengthen universal birth registration in cocoa growing areas, as a key contribution to reducing vulnerabilities associated with child labour. Lack of birth registration tends to negatively impact child labour prevalence. Children without legal identity are more at risk of becoming victims of trafficking and/or child labour than children that have their births registered. While access to school is guaranteed to all children, passing from primary to secondary school requires a birth certificate which leaves many children out of school. Out of school children are at particular risk of becoming victims of child labour without proper education opportunities for professional training and apprentice.The interventions combined policy and coordination support, service delivery strengthening in health facilities and civil registry services, late registration facilitation, and community mobilisation – implemented in close collaboration with the Ministry of the Interior (civil registry), the Ministry of Health (EPI/CPEV), local authorities, the World Cocoa Foundation, and cocoa and chocolate companies operating in the target regions of Nawa and San Pedro.Key actions included multi-stakeholder workshops to establish coordination and operational arrangements (including a Government led workshop on 31 July 2023 and a co-creation workshop in July 2025), resulting in a validated operating procedure for the regularisation of unregistered children structured around five steps: identification, community awareness, dossier preparation, legal regularisation (Law 2018 863), and monitoring and evaluation. The project also strengthened routine registration through health services by producing civil registration forms for health personnel and building capacity of immunisation staff: 68 of 113 EPI managers (CPEV) were sensitised and trained, including in the target regions and additional cocoa growing areas.To improve access and outreach, rolling equipment (motorcycles) was delivered to local authorities, notably covering sub-prefectures in Nawa and San Pedro, supporting mobility for supervision and registration activities. Community mobilisation included regional "États Généraux" in Nawa and San Pedro to diagnose bottlenecks and agree on solutions, and large scale awareness activities, including the AU/UNICEF #NoName campaign and nationwide advocacy initiatives.As a result, civil registration performance improved in the target regions: the number of children registered increased from 41,496 (2023) to 54,251 (2024), representing 12,755 additional children obtaining birth certificates.
